original_value: Short-term traffic state prediction has become an integral component of an advanced traveler information system (ATIS) in intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Accurate modeling and short-term traffic prediction are quite challenging due to its intricate characteristics, stochastic, and dynamic traffic processes. Existing works in this area follow different modeling approaches that are focused to fit speed, density, or the volume data. However, the accuracy of such modeling approaches has been frequently questioned, thereby traffic state prediction over the short-term from such methods inflicts an overfitting issue. We address this issue to accurately model short-term future traffic state prediction using state-of-the-art models via hyperparameter optimization. To do so, we focused on different machine learning classifiers such as local deep support vector machine (LD-SVM), decision jungles, multi-layers perceptron (MLP), and CN2 rule induction. Moreover, traffic states are evaluated using traffic attributes such as level of service (LOS) horizons and simple if–then rules at different time intervals. Our findings show that hyperparameter optimization via random sweep yielded superior results. The overall prediction performances obtained an average improvement by over 95%, such that the decision jungle and LD-SVM achieved an accuracy of 0.982 and 0.975, respectively. The experimental results show the robustness and superior performances of decision jungles (DJ) over other methods.

result.paraphrase: Short-term traffic state prediction is now a key part of advanced traveler information systems (ATIS) within intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Because traffic processes are complex, stochastic, and dynamic, accurate short-term modeling and prediction remain difficult. Prior studies have used different approaches aimed at fitting speed, density, or volume data, but their accuracy has often been questioned, and these methods can lead to overfitting in short-term traffic state prediction. To address this, we improve short-term future traffic state modeling through hyperparameter optimization with state-of-the-art models. The study examines several machine learning classifiers, including local deep support vector machine (LD-SVM), decision jungles, multilayer perceptron (MLP), and CN2 rule induction. Traffic states are also assessed using level of service (LOS) horizons and simple if–then rules across different time intervals. The results indicate that random sweep hyperparameter optimization produced the best outcomes. Overall prediction performance improved by more than 95% on average, with decision jungle and LD-SVM reaching accuracies of 0.982 and 0.975, respectively. The experiments demonstrate that decision jungles (DJ) are the most robust and perform better than the other methods.
